Conformity
 
A review of conformity and some of the studies that have been done on it
 
A During your childhood, there will have been some kind of craze which affected all the people in your school. It may have been to do with a particular toy or possibly a must-have item of clothing. It may have been something as simple as a type of pen or as expensive as an electronic games console. Fashion designers, toy manufacturers and anyone else involved in the retail trade love conformity. Set up a craze, especially in the young, and everyone will go for it. In fact, it's an ideal way to sell huge quantities of merchandise. The levels of conformity in consumerism are phenomenal. When you actually stand back and consider how easily we are persuaded that having certain items is the only way we can ensure peace of mind, you see what an important concept conformity is.
 
B Conformity has been described as “yielding to group pressure” (Crutchfield, 1962). However, this implies that other people put pressure on us to make us conform and this is not always the case. A better definition is given by Aronson (1976) who said it was a “change in a person's behaviour or opinions as a result of real or imagined pressure from a person or group of people”. This would make more sense, as often the pressure we feel is imagined. The person or group he refers to would have to be important to us at the time, regardless of their status.
 
C There has been considerable research on conformity. One of the first studies looked at the answers people gave when asked to estimate the number of beans in a bottle (Jenness, 1932). If you have ever entered a “guess the number” competition, you probably looked at the previous estimates made and based your judgment on what other people had guessed. This is more or less what happened in the Jenness study. First of all, he asked the respondents to give their own estimates, and then he asked them to decide a group estimate. Finally, he asked them alone again and discovered that they had stayed with the group answer.
 
D Probably the most famous study on conformity was undertaken by Asch (1951) when he created a situation where many of his subjects gave answers which were blatantly untrue, rather than contradict the people they were with. He did this by getting his subject to sit round a table with six stooges (colleagues of the experimenter) so that the subject was second to last. He showed them all a large card which had three lines of different lengths drawn on it, labelled A, B and C. He then gave them a card with a single line and asked them to match this in terms of length to one of the lines A, B or C.
 
E The stooges gave untrue responses in a number of the trials and the subjects were left in the situation where they either reported what they saw with their own eyes or conformed to the norm of the group. When the results were assessed, Asch found that in one out of every three trials where the wrong answer was given, the subject gave the same wrong answer as the stooges. This led to an average level of conformity of 32 per cent. Asch interviewed his subjects after the trials to try to find out why they conformed to an answer which was so obviously wrong. Most of them said that they did not want to cause problems within the group, although they also stated that when they did give wrong answers it made them anxious. (Asch found that when there was just one other person present who did not go along with the majority, no matter how many others there were, it was sufficient to make the subject give the right answer.)
 
F Kelman (1953) outlined three processes which can explain social conformity. The first is compliance, where subjects go along with the crowd to prevent any in-group hostility or bad feeling and to maintain group harmony. However, they do not change their own private belief. If we look back to the Asch study, we can see that the subjects were simply complying with the demands of the experimental situation but hadn't actually internalized the group's norms. They agreed in public, but dissented in private. In a process known as internalization, however, subjects do actually see the view of the group as the more valid one. They may be able to do this, for example, by convincing themselves that their eyesight is poor. Sometimes, however, subjects actually seem to change their beliefs because they want to become more like their heroes. If they really want to become part of an in-group, they will start to identify with that group and take on the group's values and beliefs, even if they are different to their own. Kelman calls this identification. It frequently happens with teenagers who want to become more like a peer group in order to be accepted, and suddenly seem to go against all the values and beliefs of their parents.
 
G So why is it that we have to conform? Some people feel confident most of the time, have high self-esteem and do not have to go along with the majority. For most of us, though, how confident we feel varies from day to day, depending on the situation we are in, and this can influence behaviour.

  • B NO

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 31–35 on your answer sheet.
Studies on conformity

In the Jenness study, people had to guess how many were in a container. Jenness found that, in most cases, people opted for an estimate given by a .

Asch asked his subjects to line lengths. To test the extent to which people would conform, he placed his subjects with colleagues who gave responses. He found that his subjects agreed with his colleagues 32% of the time, although they admitted to feeling about giving their answer.

Q27

干扰 “Simple pen (cheap) ... expensive console” 对应 “items of any value”。

句子 (Paragraph A) “It may have been something as simple as a type of pen or as expensive as an electronic games console.”

解析 题目说童年时期的热潮可以围绕**任何价值的（any value）**物品。原文A段提到：“It may have been something as simple as a type of pen or as expensive as an electronic games console（它可能像一种笔那样简单，也可能像电子游戏机那样昂贵）”，这涵盖了从便宜到昂贵的任何价值，选 YES。

Q28

解析 题目说现在的孩子比过去**更容易（more vulnerable）**受热潮影响。原文A段只提到“Set up a craze, especially in the young, and everyone will go for it（制造一个热潮，尤其是在年轻人中，每个人都会去追逐）”，并没有比较现在（now）和过去（used to be）谁更容易受影响，信息缺失，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 原文只提到了现象，没做古今对比。

Q29

解析 题目说消费者在商店里做决定的速度太快（too many quick decisions）。原文A段末尾讨论了消费者容易被说服去买东西（persuaded that having certain items is the only way...），但并没有提及做决定的速度（quick/fast），选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 文中讨论的是“easier to persuade”（容易被说服），不是“speed of decision”（决策速度）。

Q30

解析 题目说Crutchfield对从众的定义是最可靠的（most reliable）。原文B段先引用了Crutchfield的定义，然后用转折词“However”指出这并不总是情况，接着说“A better definition is given by Aronson（Aronson给出了一个更好的定义）”，这直接否定了Crutchfield是最可靠的，选 NO。

干扰 “Better definition is given by Aronson” 反驳了 “Crutchfield... is the most reliable”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...However, this implies... A better definition is given by Aronson...”

Q31

解析 题目说在Jenness的研究中，人们不得不猜测瓶子里有多少____。原文C段提到：“estimate the number of beans in a bottle（估计瓶子里豆子的数量）”，填 beans。

干扰 “Guess how many” 对应 “estimate the number of”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...estimate the number of beans in a bottle...”

Q32

解析 题目说Jenness发现，在大多数情况下，人们选择了由____给出的估算。原文C段末尾提到：“they had stayed with the group answer（他们坚持了小组的答案）”，填 group。

干扰 “Estimate given by a ______” 对应 “group estimate / answer”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...he asked them to decide a group estimate... discovered that they had stayed with the group answer.”

Q33

解析 题目说Asch要求他的受试者____线的长度。原文D段提到：“asked them to match this in terms of length to one of the lines（要求他们将这个长度与其中一条线相匹配）”，填 match。

干扰 直接对应原文动词。

句子 (Paragraph D) “...asked them to match this in terms of length...”

Q34

句子 (Paragraph E) “The stooges gave untrue responses...”

干扰 “Gave ______ responses” 对应 “gave untrue responses”。

解析 题目说他把受试者和给出____反应的同事放在一起。原文E段开头提到：“The stooges gave untrue responses（托儿给出了不真实的反应）”，填 untrue。

Q35

解析 题目说尽管他们承认在给出答案时感到____。原文E段提到：“when they did give wrong answers it made them anxious（当他们给出错误答案时，这让他们感到焦虑）”，填 anxious。

干扰 “Feeling ______” 对应 “made them anxious”。

句子 (Paragraph E) “...they also stated that when they did give wrong answers it made them anxious.”

Q36

解析 题目说“Compliance（顺从）”过程由____进行的研究结果所证实。原文F段在介绍Compliance后提到：“If we look back to the Asch study, we can see that the subjects were simply complying（如果我们回顾Asch的研究，我们可以看到受试者只是在顺从）”，填 Asch。

干扰 “Illustrated by... research conducted by” 对应 “look back to the Asch study”。

句子 (Paragraph F) “If we look back to the Asch study, we can see that the subjects were simply complying...”

Q37

句子 (Paragraph F) “In a process known as internalization...”

解析 题目要求填第二个过程的名称。原文F段提到：“In a process known as internalization（在一个被称为内化的过程中）”，填 Internalization（注意原文是美式拼写，英式为Internalisation，两者均可，雅思通常接受原文拼写）。

干扰 过程名称直接在文中出现。

Q38

解析 题目说多数人的观点被认为是____的观点。原文F段提到：“subjects do actually see the view of the group as the more valid one（受试者实际上将群体的观点视为更有效的观点）”，填 valid。

干扰 “Considered most ______ view” 对应 “see... as the more valid one”。

句子 (Paragraph F) “...subjects do actually see the view of the group as the more valid one.”

Q39

解析 题目要求填第三个过程的名称。原文F段在描述完改变信念以像英雄一样后，提到：“Kelman calls this identification（Kelman称之为认同）”，填 Identification。

干扰 过程名称。

句子 (Paragraph F) “Kelman calls this identification.”

Q40

解析 题目说这是____的典型特征。原文F段末尾提到：“It frequently happens with teenagers（这经常发生在青少年身上）”，填 teenagers。

干扰 “Typical of” 对应 “frequently happens with”。

句子 (Paragraph F) “It frequently happens with teenagers who want to become more like a peer group...”
